Documentation → Releases → 4.0.0

SATOM 4.0.0

Runbooks become Plugin Studio apps (a question that waits for a person, checks, diagnostics, Simulate) and the Process section is removed; API tokens granted per app and /api/v1/apps; Fortinet factory limits in Capacity Limits; Mass Deploy; Installed software with OS and Python upgrades that keep a rollback; a sidebar you can trim and a regrouped Settings menu.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • Before you upgrade
  • Added
  • Changed
  • Removed
  • Fixed
  • Upgrading

Released: 2026-10-25 · All releases

In short#

A major version because something was removed: the Process section, /api/v1/processes and their database tables. A runbook is now a Plugin Studio app: it can stop and wait for a person, check a device over HTTP, TCP or a read-only console command, collect diagnostics, and carry the procedure's own text on every step. Simulate rehearses the whole runbook in the editor before anyone runs it for real.

Before you upgrade#

  • A script that calls /api/v1/processes must move to /api/v1/apps with a token granted that app (see API tokens).
  • An automation that walked a process stops existing; recreate it as Run a Plugin Studio app.
  • The upgrade writes every process and run to data/process-backup-<stamp>.json (readable by the service user only) before the tables are dropped. If that file cannot be written the upgrade stops and nothing is dropped. Nothing converts a process into an app for you — rebuild the runbooks you still need from that file. See Process (removed).

Added#

  • Runbooks in Plugin Studio apps. New steps: Ask a person (the run waits and is answered on the run page), Load an appliance, HTTP check, TCP check, Console read, Appliance fact, Collect diagnostics and Activity. A check that could not look takes the error arrow, never no. Simulate in the editor, with Yes to every question.
  • API tokens granted per app and /api/v1/apps to list and run Plugin Studio apps from outside — unarmed by default, app_arm to write. New read-only capabilities metrics, findings and config_history. See API tokens.
  • Capacity Limits show Fortinet's factory limits, and your limit can be a number or a percent of them, with one default limit for every row without its own. See Capacity.
  • Mass Deploy: the newest approved version of a template to many devices; secrets are typed at deploy time. See Mass Deploy.
  • Installed software (Settings → General): every package and version per node, check for and apply OS and Python updates (never the kernel), and a rollback for every upgrade, from the web and from the console (satom execute rollback). See Settings › General.
  • Hide sidebar entries, submenus and groups (Settings → Appearance). See Appearance.
  • Plugin Studio forms list the certificates already on the FortiWebs, and any list field can be searchable.

Changed#

  • Menus: Triggers is a tab of Automation → Automations; Change Mgt Types is under Administrator → Objects; Device and System Provisioning moved to Administrator → Devices; Scout, Sentinel and Device Provisioning leave the sidebar until they are configured. See Navigation.
  • Settings regrouped one level deeper; every card has a title, starts folded and has its own anchor. Security and Change Password moved to your Profile.
  • Every table fits its screen, row actions stay on one line, and tables have an edge and a frame. The console ships its typeface (Inter).
  • Device health is grouped by ADOM; Calendar's Plan a change opens in a modal; the Wiki's Follow and Confluence buttons are on the articles.

Removed#

  • The Process section (Administrator → Process), its diagrams and runs, /api/v1/processes, the Walk a process scheduled action, automation kind and app step, XML import/export and the process_arm token capability.

Fixed#

  • Capacity no longer counts every object twice.
  • A capability-restricted API token can no longer read every recorded change; the change history no longer stores write payloads in clear.
  • Lua Studio's Delete works; 91 interface strings are translated again in de/es/fr/it.
  • A fleet rollout from the Template Library honours device bindings.

Upgrading#

Apply the update package as usual (Settings → System → Software Update, or satom execute update package), after the steps under Before you upgrade. The package upgrades a server on 3.4.7 or newer; an older server applies the v3.4.7 package first (3.3.2 or older starts with v3.3.3) and is otherwise refused at Upgrade path without any change. Rollback is a normal downgrade plus the database backup the update took; the Process tables come back only from that backup.
